g.text: Prometheus: how a metric gets from the app to an alert
Follow 1 -> 7. Red boxes are the lines that must match; arrows show where each value is used. Real files and real output (orders-api in demo-prod).
$ kubectl -n demo-prod exec deploy/orders-api -- curl localhost:8080/metrics
Rate = requests/s Errors = status 5xx Duration = latency histogram
2 + 3 The chart creates a Service and a ServiceMonitor
metrics.enabled: true in the env file
selector: # send traffic to pods with these labels
targetPort: http # the container port named "http" in deployment.yaml
- port: http # port NAME on the Service (not the number)
false = use ServiceMonitors from EVERY namespace
# Pick up ServiceMonitors / rules from every namespace, not just this Helm release.
serviceMonitorSelectorNilUsesHelmValues: false # without this, our ServiceMonitors in demo-* would be ignored
retention: 2d # keep 2 days of metrics (laptop disk)
scrapes every target every 15s, stores time series, evaluates rules
(2 targets = the 2 prod pods behind the Service, HPA min 2)
kind: ServiceMonitor # "Prometheus, please scrape this Service"
namespace: argocd # lives next to the Service it points at
selector: # find the Service by its labels
- port: http-metrics # port NAME on that Service
- record: job:http_error_ratio:rate5m # recording rule: pre-computes a query and saves it as a new metric
- alert: ErrorBudgetBurnFast # alert rule: fires when expr returns something
for: 2m # must stay true for 2 minutes before it fires (no flapping)
severity: critical # Alertmanager routes by severity (critical = page someone)
summary: "{{ $labels.job }} in {{ $labels.namespace }} is burning its error budget fast"
# runbook_url: the on-call engineer clicks this from the alert
ErrorBudgetBurnFast inactive ok HighLatencyP95 inactive ok
PodCrashLooping inactive ok ArgoAppDegraded inactive ok
Grafana (provisioned from Git): GitOps Delivery | Services (RED)
8 Latency percentiles: p50 / p95 / p99 (why the average lies)
100 requests, sorted from fastest to slowest (the promtool test traffic)
98 requests take ~1-5 ms 2 requests take 5 s
p99 = 5 s -> shows what the slowest 1% of users feel
rule: alert on percentiles, never on the average
computed once every 30s, reused by alerts AND the dashboard
expr: histogram_quantile(0.50, sum by (le, namespace, job) (rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])))
expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, namespace, job) (rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])))
expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, namespace, job) (rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])))
histogram_quantile(0.99, ...) works on BUCKETS, not on single requests
app counts requests per bucket: le=0.005 le=0.01 ... le=2.5 le=5 le=+Inf
Prometheus finds the bucket that holds the 99th request
and interpolates inside it -> an ESTIMATE
bucket boundaries decide how precise p99 can be
description: "1 in 100 requests is slower than 1s: the slow tail that users notice first."
Proof 1: promtool unit test (runs in CI)
# 98 requests under 5ms + 2 requests of 5s, every minute
p99 = 3.75s (interpolated inside the 2.5s-5s bucket) -> HighLatencyP99 FIRES
# every request was under 5ms = the first bucket (0-5ms),
"I alert on p95 and p99, not the average. p99 is what the slowest 1% feel,
and averages hide it. Prometheus estimates percentiles from histogram buckets,
so I choose bucket boundaries around my SLO, and the alert rules
are unit-tested with promtool in CI."
